Some fossils form from the body parts of organisms that get buried in sediment. If an organism stays buried for a long time, much of its body will be replaced by minerals. These minerals help preserve the structure of the organism's body as a fossil. Sometimes, small amounts of other substances, such as bits of cells and bones, may also be left behind.

Other fossils form from traces of an organism's activities, such as footprints and burrows. These traces are usually left in sediment. Over a long period of time, the sediment can get pressed together to form rock. Rocks are made of minerals.
